To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

IDO expression is seen in 14-38% of primary breast cancers and is conserved in metastatic disease; IDO is frequently co-expressed with PD-L1 in both the tumor cells and infiltrating immune cells; and, the IDO expression pattern in breast cancer is distinct from the pattern of PD-L1 expression.

IDO expression is seen in 14.5% of primary and 15.8% of metastatic breast cancers, that IDO expression in the tumor cells or the immune infiltrate is associated with PD-LI co-expression, and that IDO is conserved across primary and matched metastatic sites.

IDO expression is frequent in triple negative breast cancers and that IDO expression in tumor and tumor infiltrating immune cells is highly concordant in matched primary and metastatic breast cancers.

the expression of the enzyme IDO in breast cancer.

the expression and prognostic significance of the immune inhibitory enzyme IDO in primary breast cancers, as well as IDO fidelity in metastatic breast cancers, and the relationship between IDOs and the immune checkpoint protein PD-L1.
the expression of the immunosuppressive enzyme, IDO, in breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IDO expression is associated with high-grade, triple negative breast cancers.
IDO expression is associated with PD-LI expression and is conserved in primary and metastatic breast cancer.
IDO expression is not a major mechanism of immune evasion in triple negative breast cancers and therefore is not a good target for immunotherapy in this disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IDO expression is associated with PD-LI expression in triple-negative breast cancers, but not with metastasis.
IDO is expressed in a subset of breast cancers, particularly in triple-negative cancers.
IDO is expressed in breast cancer and may be a target for therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IDO expression is frequent in high-grade triple-negative breast cancers.
IDO expression in primary breast cancers is associated with high-grade, triple negative cancers, and is commonly coexpressed with PD-L1.
IDO expression is a feature of high-grade triple-negative breast cancer and is associated with PD-L expression in both tumor and immune cells.
